cim: CT Challenges Character.AI Plan To Auction User Info
cim_eredeti: CT Challenges Character.AI Plan To Auction User Info
szoveg_eredeti:
“Character.AI promised users they would never sell their personal information. Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats. Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground,” he said. “Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”

What’s up for sale, Tong said, includes users’ account information and chat histories – including chats in which AI characters drew children (and adults) into explicit sexual conversations, and chats in which users (including minors) shared their innermost thoughts with chatbots posing as seemingly confidential advisors, including “therapist” and “physician” characters. These conversations include intimate topics, like self-harm, eating disorders, or suicidal thoughts, Tong said. Each chat is linked to the user’s profile and metadata, including IP address and other location data, along with risk scores Character.AI gave users that it flagged.

The states are asking the court to deny the proposed sale terms, reject Smirks as the lead bidder and deny its proposed $350,000 “break-up fee” – a payment it would collect if Character.AI ends up selling to someone else. At a minimum, the states say, any sale must leave out kids’ chats and other sensitive data and include conditions that protect users.
